stem: Calculate the LCM of 101, 103 and 107.
explanation:
Write the prime factorization of the given numbers.

101 = 101\\103 = 103\\107 = 107

Take every prime factor that appears in any number and keep the highest exponent.

\text{Prime factors used: } 101, 103, 107

101^{1} \times 103^{1} \times 107^{1}

Therefore,

\operatorname{LCM}(101, 103, 107) = 1113121

Hence the LCM is 1113121.

When events repeat after fixed intervals, the first time they occur together again is the LCM of those intervals.

\text{Together again after } \operatorname{LCM}(10, 15, 20)

Using LCM,

\operatorname{LCM}(10, 15, 20) = 60

Therefore, the events will occur together again after 60.

First find the LCM of the given numbers.

\operatorname{LCM}(18, 24, 30) = 360

Every common multiple is a multiple of this LCM.

Use the counting formula.

\left\lfloor\frac{500}{360}\right\rfloor - \left\lfloor\frac{99}{360}\right\rfloor = 1

Therefore, the number of common multiples is 1.

First find the LCM of the given numbers.

\operatorname{LCM}(18, 24, 30) = 360

Every common multiple is a multiple of this LCM.

Use the counting formula.

\left\lfloor\frac{500}{360}\right\rfloor - \left\lfloor\frac{99}{360}\right\rfloor = 1

Therefore, the number of common multiples is 1.

stem: Find the number of common multiples of 8 and 12 in the interval [50, 150].
explanation:
First find the LCM of the given numbers.

\operatorname{LCM}(8, 12) = 24

Every common multiple is a multiple of this LCM.

Use the counting formula.

\left\lfloor\frac{150}{24}\right\rfloor - \left\lfloor\frac{49}{24}\right\rfloor = 4

Therefore, the number of common multiples is 4.

First find the LCM of the given numbers.

\operatorname{LCM}(8, 12) = 24

Now find the first multiple of the LCM that is greater than 70.

\left(\left\lfloor\frac{70}{24}\right\rfloor + 1\right)\times 24 = 72

Therefore, the required number is 72.
